Theme

School & learning

copy noun and verb

a copy of a text; to copy out

also copy out, copy from, cheat (copy), transcript, carbon copy

classical

Cic. Att. 8.6.1: dēinde suppositī exemplum epistulae Domitiī (Lewis & Short)
Traupman 28

exemplum, exemplī n.

noun, second declension

a copy, transcript (of a letter or text)

A copy made from an original; the original itself is exemplar or archetypum.

Other words

  • exscrībō, exscrībere, exscrīpsī, exscrīptum — copy out, write off

    verb, third conjugation: ex aliquō exscrībere · classical · Cic. Verr. 2.2.189: tabulās in forō summā hominum frequentiā exscrībō (Lewis & Short); Gell. 3.3: ex Plautī cōmoediā duōs versūs exscrīpsimus (Lewis & Short); Traupman 28: clandestīnō exscrībere, to copy by cheating

    “Don’t copy from your neighbour!” is Nōlī exscrībere ex proximō! (Traupman 33).

See also photocopy, write.

SourcesLewis & Short: exemplum · Lewis & Short: exscribo
